parts.text:
3
Which group of quantities contains only vectors?
A
acceleration, displacement, speed
B
acceleration, work, electric field strength
C
displacement, force, velocity
D
power, electric field strength, force

hints: Notice the pairs speed and velocity, and work and power in the four groups - one member of each pair has direction and the other does not.
Recall that displacement, velocity, acceleration, force and electric field strength all require a direction, while speed, distance, work, energy and power do not.
Eliminate any group that contains speed, work or power as the scalar, then check that the remaining group has three direction-dependent quantities.
walkthrough: Recall the rule: a vector has both magnitude and direction, while a scalar has magnitude only.
Sort the quantities named: vectors are displacement, velocity, acceleration, force and electric field strength; scalars are speed, work and power.
Check group A: acceleration and displacement are vectors but speed is the scalar version of velocity, so the group is mixed.
Check group B and group D: work in B and power in D are scalars because work is energy transferred and power is work per unit time, so both groups are mixed.
The remaining group contains displacement, force and velocity, and all three need a direction as well as a magnitude.

A.explanation: Acceleration and displacement are vectors but speed has magnitude only, so it is a scalar.

B.explanation: Acceleration and electric field strength are vectors but work is $force \times displacement$ in the direction of the force and has magnitude only.

C.explanation: Displacement, force and velocity all need both magnitude and direction, so all three are vectors.

D.explanation: Electric field strength and force are vectors but power is rate of doing work and has magnitude only.
